products.name: Langfuse
products.note: Open-source, framework-agnostic LLM observability: tracing, prompt management, evals, datasets; OpenTelemetry-native; acquired by ClickHouse

reading.body:
Langfuse is an open-source platform for tracing, monitoring, and evaluating LLM applications, adopted by over 50,000 companies and processing billions of observations monthly.

LLM systems generate far more observability data than traditional software: every prompt, completion, retrieval step, and tool call produces rich structured output that legacy monitoring tools cannot handle at scale. Langfuse addresses this by capturing hierarchical traces of the full execution path, allowing teams to debug, cost-optimize, and improve applications across frameworks like LangChain, Claude Agents, and Vertex AI. The platform's framework-agnostic design and OpenTelemetry compliance mean it can work across the fragmented tooling landscape that AI engineering has inherited.

For AI infrastructure, observability is already critical to the binding constraints: as models grow and systems scale, understanding where compute is spent—which prompts are expensive, which retrieval steps fail, which inference patterns waste tokens—becomes inseparable from optimization. A platform that operates at billions of observations per month is operating at the scale where decisions about inference cost and latency compound across thousands of applications.

The data does not cover pricing, deployment options, or the technical performance of Langfuse relative to alternatives. It also does not explain the scope of work ClickHouse's acquisition represents or how it affects the platform's independence or roadmap.

profile_text.body:
Langfuse is an open-source AI engineering platform, according to its own site, that helps teams build, monitor, and improve LLM applications. The company describes it as covering the full development lifecycle with tracing, prompt management, evaluations, and analytics dashboards in one place. Its site says hierarchical traces capture every LLM call, tool invocation, and retrieval step, and can be filtered by user, session, cost, latency, or custom metadata. Langfuse states that it is used by 50,000+ companies and processes billions of observations per month, and that it offers a public demo project and a free sign-up.

The site positions the product around agent evaluation and observability, with the stated aim of using production data to understand behavior, collaborate on fixes, and ship better quality at lower cost and latency. It lists integrations with Claude Code, LiteLLM, OpenClaw, the Claude Agent SDK in Python and JavaScript, LangChain, DeepAgents, OpenWebUI, Ollama, the OpenAI Agents SDK, Dify, Langflow, OpenRouter, n8n, Spring AI, Cursor, PostHog, DSPy, Amazon AgentCore, Strands Agents, LlamaIndex, Agno Agents, Temporal, ClickHouse, Mastra, Promptfoo, the Microsoft Agent Framework, Google Vertex AI, Ragas, AutoGen, and RAGflow. Langfuse describes itself as the most widely adopted open-source LLM engineering platform, aimed at developers who value open source and control over their data.

The company is tracked here as an AI governance and risk management platform, with the product described as open-source, framework-agnostic LLM observability covering tracing, prompt management, evals, and datasets, and as OpenTelemetry-native. The record also notes that Langfuse was acquired by ClickHouse. No litigation or MCP server entries are held for the company.
